assessment.nobel_worthiness: Public knowledge points to an unusually distinctive visionary voice. Blinding (the Orbitor trilogy) and Solenoid build dense, patterned prose in which memory, the body, dream and metaphysical speculation form one imaginative system. The formal ambition is high, and the work is sustained across fiction, poetry and essays.
assessment.attribution: A citation could cover the large-scale reinvention of the novel as a cosmology of consciousness and memory, grounded in the Romanian-language tradition and in poetry. The credit is to a single writer with a recognizable, consistent imaginative world.
assessment.maturity: The oeuvre has been built over several decades and has reached its fullest scale in the major late novels. Its depth and consistency suggest a mature body of work, not a single breakthrough.
uncertainties: I have not read the work directly, and this assessment rests on general public knowledge. Much of the force lies in the Romanian prose, so translation quality and corpus coverage are real uncertainties.
The poetry and early prose are less accessible in translation, so the balance between the big novels and the rest of the corpus is hard to judge.
The risk of excess or repetition across the very long works needs closer reading.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Autobiography of Red (a verse novel recasting a Greek myth) and Nox (an elegy built as a physical object) show formal invention at the borders of lyric, translation, scholarship and visual form. The voice is distinctive and the intellectual depth is considerable, with a classicist's range of reference.
assessment.attribution: A citation could cover the remaking of poetic and essayistic form through classical sources and hybrid book design. Her translations from Greek are part of the practice, but the credit is to a single author.
assessment.maturity: She has a long, steady publishing record with strong formal consistency. The open question is whether the hybrid and occasional works add up to sustained quality across the whole body.
uncertainties: Some of the work depends on the physical form of the book, and I cannot verify how fully that survives in translation.
The weight of the scholarly and translation work relative to the original poetry is uncertain.
The oeuvre is unevenly weighted toward short or occasional pieces, and I have not read it directly.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Carpentaria and The Swan Book are large, polyphonic novels with a strong claim to formal and linguistic achievement. They draw on Indigenous oral forms, ecological time and political allegory without becoming only documentary or symbolic. The voice is hard to mistake for anyone else's.
assessment.attribution: A citation could cover the remaking of the novel through Indigenous sovereignty, oral storytelling and Country, in English shaped by that experience. The credit is to one author, though her collective and nonfiction projects, such as Tracker, are part of the wider corpus.
assessment.maturity: The major novels are few but substantial and demanding. The oeuvre is still compact relative to some other candidates, so the question is depth against volume.
uncertainties: The number of major novels is small, and I cannot judge whether the later work matches the earlier.
Political and cultural significance must be kept separate from literary merit.
My knowledge of the nonfiction and of reception is general and unverified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Songs of Mihyar the Damascene and later collections reshaped modern Arabic poetry through myth, fragmentation and a sustained argument with inherited classical forms. His critical writing on Arabic poetics also shaped the field. The linguistic and formal significance is large and well known.
assessment.attribution: A citation could cover the renewal of Arabic poetic language and the dialogue between tradition and modernity. The credit is to a single poet whose essays and poems work together.
assessment.maturity: He has written across many decades with great consistency of ambition. The central achievements are long established, and later work can be assessed against them.
uncertainties: Arabic prosody and diction are hard to carry into translation, so any non-Arabic reader should be cautious about judging the poetry's quality.
I cannot verify how the translated selections represent the whole corpus.
The significance of the critical prose relative to the poetry is open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: In Three Strong Women, My Heart Hemmed In and her plays, uncanny narration and precisely controlled French prose make exclusion, family power and unstable belonging feel strange and exact. The voice is distinctive and the formal control is high.
assessment.attribution: A citation could cover the use of the uncanny to expose social and familial violence across fiction and drama. The credit is to a single writer with a coherent method.
assessment.maturity: She has a substantial body of work from early in her career and shows sustained quality. The open question is how far the later work deepens or extends the method.
uncertainties: I have not read the work directly, and the theatre is less familiar to me than the novels.
The effect of her very controlled French is partly lost in translation.
There is some risk that the method becomes repetitive across the oeuvre.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Frontier and Love in the New Millennium show a radical commitment to dreamlike narrative that unsettles psychology, space and causality. The voice is highly original and it is hard to place her in any single tradition.
assessment.attribution: A citation could cover the invention of an anti-realist, visionary mode in Chinese fiction. The credit is to one writer with an unusually consistent project.
assessment.maturity: She has a long record of publishing and a sustained, consistent method. The question is whether the method develops enough over time.
uncertainties: Only a part of the corpus is available in translation, and I cannot verify how representative it is.
Her prose may depend heavily on the rhythms of the Chinese original.
The sameness of method across many works could limit the range of the whole.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Small Lives and The Eleven are compressed, intense prose works that turn obscure lives and art history into acts of imaginative inquiry. The French is dense and the formal achievement is real. The body of work is small but concentrated.
assessment.attribution: A citation could cover the invention of a highly condensed biographical-fictional prose that questions how lives and art become legible. The credit is to a single author.
assessment.maturity: The oeuvre is slim but has been consistently admired for its quality. The main question is whether its small scale supports a claim of broad significance.
uncertainties: The quality of the prose depends heavily on the French, and the work is limited in translation.
The small size of the corpus makes the case for sustained range harder to judge.
I have not read the work directly.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Purgatory and Anteparadise are large poetic sequences that turn suffering and political violence into collective memorial form, and some of his work extends into landscape-scale and public interventions. The ambition, the voice and the link between lyric and historical catastrophe are substantial.
assessment.attribution: A citation could cover the transformation of poetry into a memorial art of the Chilean and wider Latin American experience of dictatorship. The credit is to a single poet, though some projects stretch the usual limits of the book.
assessment.maturity: He has written for decades with consistent ambition, and the central works are long established. The question is how much of the later work extends the early achievement.
uncertainties: Visual and landscape projects cannot be assessed as texts, so their literary value is hard to judge.
Translation of the poetry is uneven, and I cannot verify its coverage of the corpus.
The historical weight of the subject must be kept separate from literary merit.
